test_title: RRB Group D Previous Year Paper (Held on: 7 Oct 2022 Shift 2)
subject: general
question:
A bank offers 7.5% compound interest per annum calculated on a half-yearly basis. A customer deposits Rs. 3,600 each on 1 January and 1 July of a year. At the end of the year, the amount he would have gained by way of interest is ________.

[Give your answer correct to 2 decimal places.]
solution:
**Given:**

Rate (r) = 7.5% per annum compounded half-yearly

Principal 1 (P₁) = ₹3,600 deposited on 1 January

Principal 2 (P₂) = ₹3,600 deposited on 1 July

Time for P₁ (t₁) = 1 year

Time for P₂ (t₂) = 0.5 years

**Formula used:**

Amount (A) = P(1 + r/ⁿ)ⁿt

Where,

P = Principal

r = Annual interest rate

n = Number of times interest is compounded per year

t = Time in years

**Calculations:**

For P₁:

n = 2 (since interest is compounded half-yearly)

r/n = 7.5% / 2 = 3.75%

A₁ = 3600 (1 + ³.⁷⁵/100)²

⇒ A₁ = 3600 (1 + 0.0375)²

⇒ A₁ = 3600 (1.0375)²

⇒ A₁ = 3600 × 1.0764

⇒ A₁ = 3875.04

Interest earned from P₁ = 3875.04 - 3600 = 275.04

For P₂:

t₂ = 0.5 years

A₂ = 3600 (1 + ³.⁷⁵/100)¹

⇒ A₂ = 3600 (1 + 0.0375)¹

⇒ A₂ = 3600 × 1.0375

⇒ A₂ = 3735.00

Interest earned from P₂ = 3735.00 - 3600 = 135.00

Total interest earned = 275.04 + 135.00 = 410.04

**∴ The correct answer is option 1.**
